A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SemiSGD and PA-LFA research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation results for speed control and network routing, including convergence curves and PA-LFA versus discretization comparisons in Section 7 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 reports original results for speed control, flocking and network routing, together with sensitivity experiments and approximation comparisons in Section 7 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and update equations (1)-(6) retain the same joint semi-gradient updates, shared observations and learning rate, linear parameterizations and projections. The expanded analysis and experimental basis configurations do not change the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 retains speed control and Sioux Falls network routing and adds a flocking task with neighbor-dependent rewards and destination gathering (Appendix C.4). This substantially broadens evaluation beyond the two transportation tasks in v1.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain vanilla FPI and its entropy-regularization, fictitious-play and mirror-descent variants, plus grid discretization for the PA-LFA comparison. OMD is renamed MD; newly discussed literature does not add experimentally evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Retained experiments have substantive setting revisions: routing changes the discount factor from 0.8 to 0.5 and near-greedy inverse temperature from 100 to 1000; speed control changes its stimulus offset. The PA-LFA comparison changes its reference-grid granularity from 1/50 to 1/200, revises basis scaling and expands dimensional configurations. New sensitivity experiments also introduce controlled parameter sweeps.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled studies of FPI inner-loop iterations and regularization strength (Appendices C.3 and C.5), directly examining efficiency and stability-accuracy trade-offs. It expands the PA-LFA dimensionality analysis, while removing v1's comparison applying regularization to every routing method (Figure 8).

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over 10 independent runs with random initialization and 95% confidence regions (v1 Section 7; v2 Appendix C.1). Additional results and changed uncertainty values do not introduce a different statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds flocking and sensitivity findings and replaces results for retained experiments. For example, at dimension 25, grid/PA-LFA MSE changes from 0.22 ± 0.10 / 0.40 ± 0.04 in v1 Table 2 to 0.18 ± 0.15 / 0.06 ± 0.04 in v2 Table 1, reversing the ranking. Changed reference-grid, reward and basis settings prevent interpreting this as a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: v2 adds Assumption 5, Theorem 3, its proof and convergence-region analysis for general Lipschitz policy operators under alternative conditions (Appendix I). It also corrects suprema to minima in Lemma 9's descent proof. The earlier small-Lipschitz condition is retained and separately named Assumption 4.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions now claim conditional convergence to an equilibrium neighborhood under an alternative assumption, extending v1's theoretical contribution beyond its small-Lipschitz convergence framework. The central SemiSGD and population-aware approximation claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands explanations of regularization-induced bias, flocking failures and the benefits of basis selection. It adds a caveat about simulators requiring the full population distribution (Appendix B.2), and discusses the remaining applicability gaps and possible looseness of the new convergence-region bound (Appendix I).

D1.justification: v2 adds baseline pseudocode in Algorithm 2, an explicit temperature-selection rule, more precise basis parameters and placement, and detailed flocking simulation settings. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation. The generic supplemental-code pointer in v1's checklist disappears, without establishing that code availability itself changed.

R1.justification: The extended review and expanded comparison table in v2 Appendix A distinguish loop structures, timescales, oracle access, structural assumptions and sample complexities. Newly cited work, including Yardim et al. (2023) and Zeng et al. (2025), receives substantive comparison, substantially expanding the research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, explanatory method passages, experimental summary and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The introduction is reorganized around four methodological questions instead of two; review and motivation discussions receive dedicated appendices, and the NeurIPS checklist is removed.

P2.justification: The introductory illustration and experimental panels are separated and relocated, main results are regrouped, and new flocking and sensitivity plots are added. PA-LFA displays expand from four to eight dimensions, the literature table is relocated and enlarged, and a new theoretical correspondence table accompanies the change to ICLR formatting.

improvement.justification: The new inner-loop and regularization studies directly test explanations that v1 largely argued informally. Appendix I partially addresses the convergence limitation left open in v1, while explicitly discussing remaining gaps. Fuller experimental documentation further improves scrutiny. These are substantial gains in support and completeness, although revised benchmark settings prevent treating the changed scores as direct performance improvements.
